defect: Package selection failed for every guest at offer_lock_unavailable: svc_scd had lost EXECUTE on iam_v2.lock_auth_context_offer and the three other Gate-P lock functions.

Hotel Admin could not publish a Stay Length condition: STAY_LENGTH is the first eligibility rule type carrying a number and parseIntField did not accept json.Number, which is what the edged UseNumber decoder produces.
Editing a Service Plan silently dropped the time allowance, data allowance, idle timeout and maximum session, because the form publishes a complete revision from fields it never pre-filled.
A package left pinned to an older plan revision could only be moved by publishing another plan revision nobody wanted.
After a refused grant the portal re-enabled the same package buttons and left them on screen, so a real guest pressed three times in fourteen seconds.
The allocation-policy CHECK in migration 0064 accepted a malformed policy, because a CHECK rejects only on FALSE and every absent key evaluated to UNKNOWN.
fix: Gate-P: ROOT CAUSE was stale appliance artifacts, not source. The installed svc-scd-iamv2-guest-auth-grants.sql was 4,976 bytes with zero lock_ references against the repository 12,293; seven of eighteen Gate-P files differed and one was absent. The lock grants arrived in a704d520 and were never shipped, so a reconcile on the appliance revoked all function privileges and re-granted only the old file set. Repaired by syncing the Gate-P tree from the delivery HEAD and re-running the authoritative reconcile (gatep-grants.sql) with no ad-hoc GRANT.

parseIntField now reads every numeric shape any decoder in the system produces, through the one strict integer reader the grant snapshot already uses. Strictness is unchanged: fractional and exponent-bearing values are still refused rather than rounded.
Plan edit pre-fills all four fields, the time allowance together with the unit that makes it read 1 day, and the form is keyed on the plan so switching plans cannot publish the first plan numbers.
The repin prompt is a standing action on the plan row, listing only packages actually behind and publishing package revisions only.

A refused grant takes the offer set down and returns the guest to sign-in with the same uniform message; the retained request id means signing in again returns the SAME Auth Context, so no duplicate grant.

The CHECK predicate is wrapped in COALESCE(..., false), and the migration verify block now lifts the predicate out of the catalog with pg_get_constraintdef so it cannot drift from the real constraint.
